BiblicalUsage: Zuwa is the Aramaic word for trembling — before Nebuchadnezzar, all peoples trembled and feared, because the king's word was life or death. Darius turns it around in his decree: men must tremble and fear before the God of Daniel, because He is the living God who endures for ever. The same trembling belongs to God, not to kings.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the trembling Nebuchadnezzar demanded was owed to God all along, and Darius finally said so.
